content.title: About
content.content: Grapes are the edible berries of the grapevine (Vitis vinifera), cultivated in temperate regions worldwide. Raw grapes have a sweet‑tart flavor and a juicy, crisp texture. They are eaten fresh, added to salads, desserts, juices, and used in winemaking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grapes are one of the oldest cultivated plants, with cultivation dating back over 8,000 years.
There are more than 8,000 grape varieties, differing in color, taste, and berry size.
Grape seeds contain polyphenols that have antioxidant properties.
Vineyards can live over a hundred years; some ancient vines in Europe are considered cultural heritage.
Grapes were called the “fruit of the gods” in ancient Greek and Roman mythology.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Grapes contain resveratrol, quercetin, and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Flavonoids in grapes improve vascular function and may lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber in the skin and pulp promotes healthy digestion and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and other phytochemicals enhance the immune system.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to grapes, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Fresh grapes are high in natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Unwashed grapes may carry pesticide residues; it is recommended to rinse them thoroughly before eating.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidity of grapes can irritate the stomach in those sensitive to acidic foods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat grapes raw as a snack, add them to salads, yogurts, cereals, use in desserts and smoothies. They can be frozen for sorbets or incorporated into sauces. Both skin‑on and skin‑off grapes are nutritious.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store grapes in the refrigerator in their original bag or a perforated container to allow airflow. Properly stored, they stay fresh for 1–2 weeks. Remove any spoiled berries to prevent the rest from deteriorating.
